assessments.role: transferable method evidence on additive effects in operando/kinetic observables
assessments.claim: In a CN electrode study, transient absorption at 850 nm and photocurrent measurements linked higher pH to longer electron lifetime via facilitated hole removal, and TEOA further increased the transient absorption signal.
assessments.transfer_limit: Not a Co(II)-bipyridine CO2-reduction system; electrode/photoanode context and material-specific charge transport may not transfer quantitatively. Supports testing donor/additive effects on charge separation or hole scavenging, not product selectivity mechanisms directly.
assessments.reason: Provides an identifiable observation that TEOA changes a charge-carrier observable, relevant for designing characterization to compare TEA versus TEOA effects, but the platform mismatch is substantial.

assessments.transfer_limit: Electrocatalytic heterogeneous CO2RR review rather than homogeneous photocatalytic Co-bipyridine catalysis; supports characterization design principles and assignment controls, not direct mechanistic claims for the target system. assessments.role: direct evidence that TEOA can participate non-innocently yet CO can still derive from CO2
assessments.claim: A 2023 homogeneous photochemical study investigated TEOA impacts and reported CO formation in aqueous TEOA solution without other additives under light irradiation, while isotope labeling confirmed the CO product originated from CO2 rather than TEOA decomposition.
assessments.transfer_limit: Catalyst/system identity is not given in this snippet and differs from the Co(II)-bipyridine comparison. It does not compare TEA versus TEOA, but it directly motivates origin controls and consideration of TEOA decomposition-coupled chemistry.
assessments.reason: This is a reported observation with an origin control. It is relevant because TEOA-specific chemistry could confound interpretation of donor effects, yet the isotope result bounds one alternative explanation.

assessments.role: cross-system evidence that TEA can alter rate without changing product distribution plus product-origin control practice
assessments.claim: In CuOx@p-ZnO photocatalytic CO2 reduction, adding TEA was reported to enhance only the reaction rate without changing the reaction pathway/product distribution, and a separate 13CO2 GC-MS experiment was conducted with TEA as hole scavenger.
assessments.transfer_limit: Heterogeneous Cu/ZnO system, not molecular Co(II)-bipyridine. TEA behavior may differ across catalysts and media, so transfer is limited to hypothesis framing and control selection rather than expected outcome.
assessments.reason: Provides negative/limiting evidence against assuming amine donors necessarily change selectivity, and shows a relevant isotopic-origin control in a photocatalytic context.

assessments.role: directly relevant comparator formulation evidence in a cobalt photocatalytic CO2-reduction system
assessments.claim: A binuclear cobalt photocatalytic CO2-reduction system used [Ru(phen)3]2+ as photosensitizer and 0.3 M TEOA in CO2-saturated CH3CN/H2O (4:1) under 450 nm irradiation for 10 h.
assessments.transfer_limit: Catalyst is a binuclear cobalt cryptate rather than the researcher's Co(II)-bipyridine complex, so mechanistic transfer is limited. However, it is chemically close in being a homogeneous cobalt photocatalytic CO2-reduction system with explicit donor, PS, medium, and light conditions.
assessments.reason: Among the supplied snippets, this is one of the most directly usable cobalt-system formulations for defining a literature-supported platform around TEOA and common photocatalytic components.

assessments.role: transferable mechanistic contrast on proton-source dependence
assessments.claim: For Mn-based molecular CO2-reduction catalysts, replacing inert gas with 1 atm CO2 typically gives no catalytic current without a proton source, whereas catalytic current is generally observed when CO2 is introduced together with an external Brønsted acid.
assessments.transfer_limit: Electrochemical Mn systems are not the target photocatalytic Co(II)-bipyridine system, so transfer is conceptual only. It supports testing whether TEA/TEOA effects arise partly through proton-source or proton-management differences, not that the same mechanism operates.
assessments.reason: Provides a clear mechanistic contrast emphasizing proton-source dependence, useful for framing competing explanations for donor-dependent CO/H2 distributions.
